label: L-06
severityAgreementNote: AGREES with the incoming Low. Medium was tested explicitly on the 'leak value with stated assumptions' limb and DECLINED on a marginal-capability test that this stage established from the minter's source rather than inheriting (judgementCalls JC-02).
title: The caller, not the protocol, picks WHICH registered stablecoin to pair with, and the pairing is by quantity rather than value, so a depegged stable whose manually-maintained exchangeRate has not yet been cut is every annihilator's dominant choice
preExistingLabel: PRE-EXISTING at c91bc1a, NOT delta-induced by story-003. This must be stated in the write-up or a reader will mistake it for a story-003 regression. story-003 touched neither toStableAmount nor the caller's freedom to choose `stable`.
fingerprintNote: Carried VERBATIM from the sanitizer; not re-derived at this stage.
c4Criterion: QA/Low - 'state handling' / operational-configuration hazard. It does not reach Medium because the value-leak channel it describes is already fully open, permissionlessly and in unbounded size, on a path that does not involve Antimatter at all, so Antimatter contributes no marginal capability to it.

classification.assetImpact: POTENTIAL protocol-side dilution, not user loss: phUSD minted against collateral whose market value is below the registered exchangeRate is unbacked, and per the run-01 finding that is real dilution rather than opportunity cost. The channel is Antimatter-adjacent, however, not Antimatter-specific - see marginalCapability.
attackPath: 1. A registered stablecoin S depegs to $0.60. Its registered exchangeRate is still 1e18 because updateExchangeRate is a manual, owner-only act (PhusdStableMinter.sol:138) with no staleness bound, no oracle and no timestamp read anywhere on the annihilate path (zero `block.` hits in src/, verified).

2. toStableAmount (:283-302) is a pure decimal rescale with NO price input: 1e18 of antimatter pairs with exactly 1 whole unit of whichever registered stable the caller names, regardless of what that unit is worth.

3. `stable` is a free caller-supplied parameter, so every annihilator's dominant strategy during the latency window is to pair against S - buying the phUSD half at a discount to par - rather than against a stable trading at $1.00.
4. The protocol receives S at par against a phUSD mint priced at the stale rate.
classification.marginalCapability: DECISIVE, and established at this stage from source rather than assumed. PhusdStableMinter.mint (PhusdStableMinter.sol:203) is PERMISSIONLESS - `external nonReentrant` with no access control, gated only on !paused, config.enabled and the rolling 24h cap. Anyone holding the depegged S can mint phUSD directly against the stale rate, in whatever size the daily cap allows, without holding a single unit of antimatter. The stale-rate mint is therefore ALREADY fully available, and it is available in strictly larger size than the annihilate path, which is additionally bounded by the caller's antimatter balance. What annihilate adds is only that the annihilator's own asset SELECTION is unconstrained - a real asymmetry, but one that adds no dilution capability an attacker did not already possess more cheaply. Under the same marginal-capability test the pipeline applied to L-04 in run-02, that holds this at Low.
classification.likelihood: Requires a genuine depeg of a registered stable AND owner latency in cutting its rate AND an actor choosing to use it. All three are plausible; none is observable at HEAD.
assumptions: The owner has not yet cut its exchangeRate - the manual-maintenance latency window.
More than one stablecoin is registered, so a choice exists at all. Not established at HEAD; Antimatter is not wired into staging (run-01).
classification.externalRequirements: A market event (the depeg) plus owner response latency. Both are outside the protocol's control and neither is caused by this code.
classification.rootCauseLocation: The absence of any staleness bound on exchangeRate lives in the NESTED dependency PhusdStableMinter (lib/antimatter/lib/phUSD-stable-minter/), which is outside first-party scope. It is parked as MR-03-D-08 rather than filed against the dependency. What is filed here is the first-party contribution only: that Antimatter hands asset selection to the caller and pairs by quantity.

wontFixDisclosure.MANDATORY: This block must appear IN the write-up, verbatim, including the prior entry's label. Do not paraphrase and do not omit it.
wontFixDisclosure.priorTriageReasonVERBATIM: The stable leg is handled by phUSD-minter stable security. The exchange rate is there in case of a depeg. But the 1:1 with antimatter is unrelated. The antimatter was earned elsewhere. It already has its value. phUSD is just realizing that.
wontFixDisclosure.isThisARefile: NO. M-04 is WITHIN-asset re-pricing - the rate re-prices only the stable leg of one named asset. This is CROSS-asset SELECTION: the caller names which registered stable to pair, and toStableAmount is a pure decimal rescale with no price input. Different mitigation; no ledger fingerprint covers selection.
wontFixDisclosure.basisForRaisingItAnyway: The owner's triage explicitly names the depeg case as KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY HANDLED ('the exchange rate is there in case of a depeg'). What the triage does not address, and could not have, is (a) the LATENCY of that manual handling - no staleness bound, no oracle, no timestamp anywhere on the path - and (b) that the CALLER, not the protocol, chooses the asset, which converts a latency window into a dominant strategy.
wontFixDisclosure.doesNotOverride: This finding does NOT re-weigh, override or reopen M-04 (abe4305ac8f0c44f), which remains wont-fix at the owner's human-set disposition. It is filed as adjacent-but-distinct at LOW.

justification: LOW. The C4 Medium limb genuinely in play is 'leak value with a hypothetical attack path with stated assumptions, but external requirements', and I am not pretending it is unengaged: unbacked phUSD is real dilution rather than opportunity cost, and the caller-chooses-asset property does convert a symmetric latency window into an asymmetric one. Two things hold it at Low, and the first is decisive. (1) MARGINAL CAPABILITY IS ZERO. PhusdStableMinter.mint is permissionless and unconditioned on antimatter, so the identical stale-rate mint is already open to anyone holding the depegged stable, in strictly larger size than the annihilate path permits. Escalating a finding whose channel is already fully open elsewhere - and whose root cause, the missing staleness bound, sits in a nested dependency outside first-party scope - would attribute to Antimatter a capability it does not add. (2) THE CONJUNCTION IS ASSERTED, NOT OBSERVED. It needs a real depeg AND unresolved owner latency AND at least two registered stables to choose between; none of the three is established at HEAD, and a conjunction of unobserved terms is what C4 calls hand-wavy. What survives, and is genuinely first-party and genuinely worth an owner's eye, is the operational point: annihilate's asset selection is unconstrained by design, so the latency window on a manually-maintained rate is adversarially selected against rather than merely exposed. That is an operational-hazard Low with a minter-side or registration-side mitigation, and it is filed with the M-04 wont-fix disclosed rather than silently re-filed under a new fingerprint.
recommendation: Protocol-side, and outside this contract's reach in the primary case: put a staleness bound (or an oracle cross-check) on PhusdStableMinter's exchangeRate, so a rate that has not been refreshed within a bounded window fails closed rather than continuing to quote par. First-party mitigations if that is not available: restrict the registered set to a single stable, or gate annihilate's `stable` parameter behind an owner-maintained allowlist narrower than the minter's registry, so the caller's selection freedom is bounded by policy rather than by whatever happens to be registered.

sourceVerification: src/Antimatter.sol:283-302 (toStableAmount) read at 3a96fb7: it resolves the minter's registered decimals, cross-checks them against the token's own decimals(), and rescales by 10**(18-decimals). No price, no rate, no timestamp.
src/Antimatter.sol:226 - `stable` is a free caller-supplied parameter of annihilate.

PhusdStableMinter.sol:203 `function mint(address stablecoin, uint256 amount) external nonReentrant` - PERMISSIONLESS. Verified at this stage by reading the nested source and by grepping the file's access-control surface: onlyOwner appears on registerStablecoin, updateExchangeRate (:138), setStablecoinEnabled, approveYS and setMaxMintPerDay, and on none of the user functions. This is the basis of the marginal-capability test.
PhusdStableMinter.sol:138 `updateExchangeRate ... external onlyOwner` - manual, no staleness field written or read.
